title: 30 Cmd-N at key-repeat speed with a Cmd-Shift-W after every third leave 20 new workspaces, numbered without a gap, in press order, with no refusal (cx-7cit9)
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab

steps.note: the scenario of scripts/cmux-next/rapid-workspace-e2e.py (kept): the workspaces before the burst

presses 1-15 with their closes. One debug.key request per press, back to back: every press is faster than the create before it, so each Cmd-Shift-W lands on a workspace still being created (the script's 33 ms interval is a floor, not the bug). With no settled checkpoint, burst-2 follows at once: one key step takes at most 32 keys

presses 16-30 with their closes. New Tab page workspaces show at once as stand-ins (WorkspaceSpawner.shown) and leave the intent log when the daemon has them, so the wait and the settle end after the last create of the window's lane (WorkspaceLanes)

invariants: the topology at after-burst lists the workspaces of launched plus 20 new ones, and liveObjects.workspaceModels grew by 20: each Cmd-Shift-W closed exactly the workspace its window showed at the press
the new workspaces' names are workspace-N with consecutive N (the daemon numbers them in press order)
intents.totals.refused is the same at launched and after-burst, and overlays at after-burst holds no refusalHud: no 'no workspace <uuid>' refusal
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
ids stay stable unless the step created or closed them (I2)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: the sidebar's row order against the daemon's (debug.sidebar_rows): the sidebar facet (p15-oracle-036) has no provider on the base, so the press order is read from the names, not from the rows
the New Tab page's omnibar suggestions (debug.new_tab state): no facet records them
a toast that came and went during the burst: a checkpoint sees only the state after it; the refused total covers the refusal HUD
the script's window captures (debug.window_snapshot); captures are the media tours' job
